policy: Grouped by source video: no recording appears in both splits. Frozen once; the held-out split is to be executed a single time, after development against the dev split is complete.

refrozen.reason: Four cases were withdrawn from the corpus because they ran against tears_of_steel_61min.webm, which was the 12.2-minute Blender film concatenated five times rather than an hour-long recording. The corpus went from 39 cases to 35, so corpus_fingerprint had to be recut.
refrozen.what_changed: Only the dev side. All four withdrawn cases were dev cases, and the held-out side is the split frozen on 2026-09-05: same 12 cases, same 6 recordings, same fingerprint. It has still never been executed. Dev went from 27 cases over 6 recordings to 23 over 5.
refrozen.known_limitation: The corpus now holds exactly one mixed_av case and it sits in the held-out split, so the dev side cannot exercise that category at all. The original design requirement that both sides cover every query category is arithmetically unsatisfiable at n=35 and is not met. It was not weakened to hide that: the requirement now tested is that every category with at least two cases appears on both sides, with singleton categories recorded explicitly here. Authoring more mixed_av cases and recutting is the real fix.

history.detail: Four cases were removed from data/eval/long-video-quality.jsonl because they ran against tears_of_steel_61min.webm, which was the 12.2-minute Blender film concatenated five times rather than an hour-long recording. The dataset is now 35 cases, not the 39 this split was frozen over, so corpus_fingerprint no longer matches.
